question:
Select the most appropriate synonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

Confession had always rested on a clear distinction between mortal and (venial) sins.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pardonable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Venial means slight, minor and easily forgiven or excused; in Christian theology a venial sin is one that can be pardoned, as opposed to a *mortal* sin. (क्षम्य, मामूली)

◦ Pardonable means able to be forgiven or excused — an exact match for "venial". (क्षमा योग्य)

◦ The sentence contrasts "mortal" (deadly, unforgivable) with "venial", so the blank word must mean the opposite of mortal.

◦ Correct: Confession had always rested on a clear distinction between mortal and pardonable sins.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Genial means friendly and cheerful (मिलनसार) — it sounds like "venial" but is unrelated in meaning.

• Major means great or important; it is closer to "mortal" and destroys the contrast.

• Intolerable means unbearable (असहनीय) — the opposite of pardonable.

NOTE

• Synonyms of venial: excusable, forgivable, minor, trivial, slight.

• Antonyms of venial: mortal, unforgivable, inexcusable, grave, heinous.

• Do not confuse venial (pardonable) with venal (corrupt, open to bribery).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Sam knew who those people were; the figure in front was ______ his cousin.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. unmistakeably.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adverb to modify the sentence — "the figure in front was ______ his cousin" means it was beyond any doubt his cousin. (निस्संदेह)

◦ Unmistakeably/unmistakably = so clear that there can be no mistake; it fits the first clause "Sam knew who those people were".

◦ Correct: Sam knew who those people were; the figure in front was unmistakeably his cousin.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "by mistake" means accidentally/in error — it reverses the intended sense of certainty.

• "at mistake" is not a valid English collocation; the correct phrase is *by mistake*.

• "mistaken of" is ungrammatical; the correct forms are *mistaken for* or *mistaken about*.

NOTE

• Useful certainty adverbs: undoubtedly, unquestionably, undeniably, indisputably, definitely.

• Fixed phrases with mistake: make a mistake, by mistake, mistake A for B.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Insigt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is Insight — in + sight — meaning a deep understanding of a person or thing. (अंतर्दृष्टि)

◦ The printed word "Insigt" drops the silent h, so it is misspelt.

◦ Correct: The report offers valuable insight into consumer behaviour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Supply (आपूर्ति) is correctly spelt — noun/verb meaning to provide.

• Optical (दृष्टि संबंधी) is correctly spelt — relating to sight or light.

• Cares (परवाह करता है) is correctly spelt — third person singular of "care".

NOTE

• Words with silent gh: sight, night, height, weight, thought, brought.

• Commonly misspelt SSC words: accommodation, occurrence, embarrass, maintenance, privilege, foreign.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Rapid climate warming in / the tundra biome have been linked / to increasing shrub dominance.
option_3: the tundra biome have been linked
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the tundra biome have been linked.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The real subject of the sentence is "Rapid climate warming", which is singular, so the verb must be has been linked, not "have been linked". (कर्ता-क्रिया समन्वय)

◦ "in the tundra biome" is a prepositional phrase; the noun inside a prepositional phrase never controls the verb — this is the rule of proximity trap.

◦ Correct: Rapid climate warming in the tundra biome has been linked to increasing shrub dominance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No error" is wrong because the sentence does contain a subject–verb agreement error.

• Option 2 "Rapid climate warming in" is correct — a singular uncountable subject with a preposition.

• Option 4 "to increasing shrub dominance" is correct — "link to" is the right preposition and "increasing" is a participial adjective.

NOTE

• Ignore words between the subject and verb: *The box of chocolates is on the table.*

• Similar structures: *A list of items has been sent.* / *The quality of the mangoes was poor.*

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Farms are increasingly turning to automation for ______ reasons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. many.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reasons" is a plural countable noun, and the determiner used before plural countable nouns to show a large number is many. (अनेक)

◦ Much and little are used only with uncountable nouns (much water, little milk), so they cannot qualify "reasons".

◦ Correct: Farms are increasingly turning to automation for many reasons.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "most reasons" would mean *the majority of a known set of reasons*, which the sentence has not introduced — it is contextually wrong here.

• "much reasons" is ungrammatical because *much* never precedes a plural countable noun.

• "little reasons" is ungrammatical for the same reason; the countable form would be *few reasons*, which reverses the meaning.

NOTE

• Countable → many, few, a few, fewer, number of. Uncountable → much, little, a little, less, amount of.

• *Fewer* + countable (fewer cars) vs *less* + uncountable (less traffic).

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

I didn't have time to give them proof.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. evidence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Proof means facts or information that establish that something is true. (प्रमाण, सबूत)

◦ Evidence carries the same meaning — the body of facts that supports a conclusion, so it is the closest synonym.

◦ Correct: I didn't have time to give them evidence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Guess means an estimate made without sure information (अनुमान) — the opposite of proof.

• Snap means a sudden sharp sound, a quick photograph, or to break suddenly (चटकना) — unrelated.

• Charge means an accusation, a price, or to load (आरोप/शुल्क) — an accusation is what proof is needed for, not proof itself.

NOTE

• Synonyms of proof: evidence, confirmation, verification, testimony, corroboration, substantiation.

• Related legal collocations: burden of proof, conclusive evidence, circumstantial evidence.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Participate in a mock interview to prepare for ______ on your feet and formulating answers under pressure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. thinking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to think on your feet" means to react and make decisions quickly and effectively without prior preparation. (तुरंत सोचकर निर्णय लेना)

◦ It pairs naturally with "formulating answers under pressure", which is exactly what a mock interview trains.

◦ The preposition "for" requires a gerund, and "thinking" is the gerund form.

◦ Correct: Participate in a mock interview to prepare for thinking on your feet and formulating answers under pressure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "blocking on your feet" is not an English idiom and gives no sensible meaning.

• "cursing on your feet" is meaningless and contradicts the professional context of an interview.

• "building on your feet" is not an idiom; the existing idiom is *build on something* (to develop further).

NOTE

• Related "feet" idioms: stand on one's own feet (be independent), get cold feet (lose nerve), find one's feet (settle in), drag one's feet (delay).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

She blew out the candle and gone to sleepy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. went to sleep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first verb "blew" is in the simple past tense, so the verb joined by "and" must also be in the simple past — hence went, not "gone". (समानांतर काल)

◦ "Gone" is the past participle (V3) and cannot stand alone without an auxiliary such as *has/have/had*.

◦ The fixed phrase is go to sleep (noun "sleep"), never "go to sleepy" — *sleepy* is an adjective.

◦ Correct: She blew out the candle and went to sleep.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "went to sleeps" wrongly pluralises the uncountable noun "sleep".

• "go to sleep" is the present/base form and breaks tense parallelism with "blew".

• "No improvement" is wrong because the printed part "gone to sleepy" has both a tense error and a word-form error.

NOTE

• Parallelism rule: verbs joined by *and/or/but* must share the same tense and form — *He came, saw and conquered.*

• V1–V2–V3: go – went – gone; blow – blew – blown; sleep – slept – slept.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

At all costs
option_2: Whatever is needed to achieve something
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Whatever is needed to achieve something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "at all costs" means regardless of the price, effort or sacrifice involved — no matter what it takes. (हर हाल में, किसी भी कीमत पर)

◦ It is used to stress absolute determination: *We must avoid a leak at all costs.*

◦ Correct: The team was determined to win the final at all costs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Not to be trifled with" describes a person who must be taken seriously — that is the idiom *not to be trifled with*, not *at all costs*.

• "To be master of" means to have complete command over something — unrelated to cost or sacrifice.

• "An expensive purchase" is a literal reading of the word "cost" and misses the idiomatic sense.

NOTE

• Similar idioms: by hook or by crook, come what may, at any price, move heaven and earth.

• Note the contrast: at all costs (determination) vs at cost (at the price paid, without profit).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Tax dispute settlement might not work out in the desired scale.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. might not work out in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed collocation is "on a/the scale", not "in the scale" — we always say *on a large scale*, *on a national scale*, *on the desired scale*. (पैमाने पर)

◦ So the preposition in in the segment "might not work out in" must be replaced by on.

◦ Correct: Tax dispute settlement might not work out on the desired scale.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "the desired scale." is correct — the definite article with a past-participle adjective is fine.

• Option 3 "Tax dispute settlement" is a correct noun phrase acting as the subject.

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong because the sentence does contain a preposition error.

NOTE

• Prepositions with "scale": on a large/small/global scale, to scale, scale of 1 to 10.

• Other tested collocations: on purpose, on time, in time, at length, by chance, in vain.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A unit to measure light
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Lumen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A lumen (lm) is the SI unit of luminous flux, i.e. the measure of the total visible light emitted by a source. (प्रकाश मापने की इकाई)

◦ Bulb packaging states brightness in lumens, which is why "a unit to measure light" = lumen.

◦ Correct: A unit to measure light is called a lumen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Watt is the unit of power (rate of energy use), not of light output.

• Horse-power is a non-SI unit of power, chiefly used for engines (1 hp ≈ 746 W).

• Ampere is the SI unit of electric current.

NOTE

• Light-related units: lumen (luminous flux), lux (illuminance = lumen/m²), candela (luminous intensity), candle power.

• Other one-word substitutions: Ammeter (measures current), Barometer (pressure), Seismograph (earthquakes), Hygrometer (humidity).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Cell phones keeps loved ones and those nearly them well connected.
option_4: keep loved ones and those near
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. keep loved ones and those near.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "Cell phones" is plural, so the verb must be the plural form keep, not "keeps". (कर्ता-क्रिया समन्वय)

◦ "Nearly" is an adverb meaning *almost*; what is required here is the adjective/preposition near, meaning *close by* — "those near them".

◦ Correct: Cell phones keep loved ones and those near them well connected.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because the printed part has both a verb-agreement error and a wrong word form.

• Option 2 "keeping loved and nearly" leaves the sentence without a finite verb and keeps the wrong word "nearly".

• Option 3 "kept love and near" shifts to the past tense unnecessarily and replaces the noun phrase "loved ones" with "love".

NOTE

• Adjective vs adverb pairs: near/nearly, hard/hardly, late/lately, high/highly — the -ly form usually has a different meaning.

• *He works hard* (with effort) vs *He hardly works* (almost not at all).

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Discreet
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Open.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Discreet means careful and prudent in speech or action so as to avoid attention or giving offence — i.e. secretive, tactful, unobtrusive. (विवेकपूर्ण, गुप्त)

◦ Its opposite is being open — frank, public and holding nothing back. (खुला, स्पष्टवादी)

◦ Correct: She was discreet about the news, whereas her brother was completely open about it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Release means to set free or let go (मुक्त करना) — it is not related to discretion.

• Zenith means the highest point or peak (शिखर); its antonym is *nadir*.

• Lose means to fail to keep or win (खोना); its antonym is *find/win*.

NOTE

• Synonyms of discreet: tactful, prudent, circumspect, cautious, guarded.

• Antonyms of discreet: indiscreet, open, blatant, careless, tactless.

• Do not confuse discreet (tactful) with discrete (separate, distinct).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

He had moved about two inches when several things happened in very ______ succession.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. quick.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The standard collocation is "in quick succession", meaning one event following another rapidly, with very little gap. (तेजी से एक के बाद एक)

◦ The context — "several things happened" while he moved only two inches — demands the idea of speed, which "quick" supplies.

◦ Correct: He had moved about two inches when several things happened in very quick succession.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "brief succession" is not an accepted collocation; *brief* describes duration, not the gap between repeated events.

• "desperate" means hopeless or reckless (हताश) and does not describe a sequence of events.

• "absurd" means ridiculous or illogical (बेतुका) and does not fit the neutral narrative tone.

NOTE

• Fixed collocations with succession: in quick succession, in rapid succession, in close succession.

• Other set phrases: in short supply, in high demand, in full swing, in due course.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Rolling in cash
option_1: Have a large quantity of money
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Have a large quantity of money.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "rolling in cash" (also *rolling in money/dough/it*) means to be extremely rich, to have plenty of money. (बहुत धनवान होना)

◦ The image is of someone with so much money that he could roll about in it.

◦ Correct: After the company was sold, the founders were rolling in cash.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "A business magnate" names a *person* (a tycoon); the idiom describes a state of wealth, not an occupation.

• "Buying things on interest" refers to credit purchases and has no link with the idiom.

• "To borrow a costly attire" is a literal, unrelated meaning invented as a distractor.

NOTE

• Similar wealth idioms: born with a silver spoon in one's mouth, make a killing, loaded, live in the lap of luxury.

• Poverty idioms often paired in exams: hand to mouth, on the breadline, tighten one's belt.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

Destruction of a fetus
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Feticide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Feticide (foeticide) literally means the killing or destruction of a fetus — from Latin *fetus* + *-cide* (to kill). (भ्रूण हत्या)

◦ The suffix -cide always denotes an act of killing, e.g. *homicide*, *suicide*, *genocide*.

◦ Correct: The law strictly punishes female feticide.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Fratricide is the killing of one's own brother (भ्रातृहत्या).

• Ellipse is a geometrical figure — an oval closed curve; it has nothing to do with killing.

• Abhor is a verb meaning to hate or detest intensely (घृणा करना), not a one-word substitution for a killing.

NOTE

• Common *-cide* words: matricide (mother), patricide (father), infanticide (infant), regicide (king), uxoricide (wife), genocide (a race), germicide (germs), insecticide (insects).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

The benefits of rebuilding healthy, fertile soil are clear.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject is "The benefits" (plural), so the plural verb are is correct — the intervening phrase "of rebuilding healthy, fertile soil" does not affect agreement. (कर्ता-क्रिया समन्वय)

◦ Rebuilding is a gerund correctly placed after the preposition "of", and it takes the object "healthy, fertile soil".

◦ "healthy, fertile" are two coordinate adjectives correctly separated by a comma before the noun "soil".

◦ Correct: The benefits of rebuilding healthy, fertile soil are clear. (no change needed)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "healthy, fertile soil" is grammatically sound; *soil* is uncountable and needs no article here.

• Option 2 "The benefits of rebuilding" correctly uses preposition + gerund.

• Option 4 "are clear." correctly matches the plural subject *benefits*.

NOTE

• Rule: the verb agrees with the head noun of the subject, not with the noun nearest to it.

• *The causes of the accident are unknown.* / *The cause of the accidents is unknown.*

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

The peach-tree is most productive when the roots are kept near the surface.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. futile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Productive means yielding good results, producing plenty — fruitful. (उत्पादक, फलदायी)

◦ Futile means producing no useful result; pointless and unproductive, hence the exact antonym. (व्यर्थ, निष्फल)

◦ Correct: All his efforts to revive the dying peach-tree proved futile.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lush means growing thickly and luxuriantly (हरा-भरा) — a synonym-side word, not an antonym.

• Potent means powerful and effective (शक्तिशाली) — again close in sense to productive.

• Fertile means capable of producing abundant growth (उपजाऊ) — a direct synonym of productive.

NOTE

• Synonyms of futile: vain, fruitless, useless, ineffective, unavailing, abortive.

• Antonyms of futile: useful, effective, productive, fruitful, worthwhile.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

(Beside myself, the only English people) there were Keith and Doreen.
option_1: Besides I, the only English speaking people
option_3: Besides myself, the only English people
option_4: Beside me, the only English people
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Besides myself, the only English people.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Besides means "in addition to / apart from", whereas beside means "by the side of". The sentence lists people in addition to the speaker, so besides is required. (के अलावा बनाम के बगल में)

◦ After "besides" the reflexive/emphatic form myself is idiomatic in this construction, and the rest of the phrase "the only English people" is retained unchanged.

◦ Correct: Besides myself, the only English people there were Keith and Doreen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Besides I" is wrong because a preposition must be followed by an object pronoun (*me*), not the subject pronoun *I*; it also adds "speaking", changing the meaning.

• Option 2 "No substitution required" is wrong because the printed "Beside" is the wrong word.

• Option 4 keeps the wrong preposition "Beside" (= next to), which makes the sentence illogical.

NOTE

• Beside = at the side of: *He sat beside her.* Besides = in addition to / moreover: *Besides English, she knows French.*

• Idiom: beside oneself (with joy/anger) = extremely upset or excited.

question: Four sentences are given, out of which three have spelling errors. Choose the sentence with all correctly spelt words.
option_1: I don't know weather to eat it or rubb it on.
option_2: Goodbye untill later now, foks. Have a good night.
option_4: Had I known what was coming, I could have prepared myself better.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Had I known what was coming, I could have prepared myself better.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every word in option 4 — *known, coming, prepared, myself, better* — is spelt correctly, and the inverted conditional (Had I known… I could have prepared) is grammatically sound.

◦ Correct: Had I known what was coming, I could have prepared myself better.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 has rubb (correct: *rub*) and uses weather where the correct word is whether.

• Option 2 has untill (correct: *until*) and foks (correct: *folks*).

• Option 3 has humerous (correct: *humorous*).

NOTE

• Homophone alert: weather (मौसम) vs whether (चाहे/क्या) vs wether (a castrated ram).

• Single vs double letters: *until* (one l), *fulfil/fulfill*, *travelled* (BrE) / *traveled* (AmE), *humorous* (humour → humorous, the *u* is dropped).

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By the (1) ______ we reach puberty, the world has reached us and (2) ______ us to a greater extent than we realize. (3) ______ family, friends, school, and society in general (4) ______ -by word and example-how to be. But people (5) ______ leaders at that moment when they decide for themselves how to be.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. time.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed conjunctive phrase is "by the time", which introduces a clause meaning *before or when a particular event happens*. (जब तक)

◦ Only "time" collocates with "by the … we reach puberty"; the structure is by the time + subject + verb.

◦ Correct: By the time we reach puberty, the world has reached us…

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "by the moment" is not an English phrase; the accepted forms are *at the moment* and *the moment (that)*.

• "by the age" would need a number — *by the age of twelve* — not a clause.

• "by the era" is unidiomatic; *era* denotes a long historical period, not a personal milestone.

NOTE

• Note the tense rule: By the time + present tense → main clause in present perfect/future perfect: *By the time he arrives, we will have finished.*

• Similar time connectors: as soon as, no sooner … than, hardly … when, the moment.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By the (1) ______ we reach puberty, the world has reached us and (2) ______ us to a greater extent than we realize. (3) ______ family, friends, school, and society in general (4) ______ -by word and example-how to be. But people (5) ______ leaders at that moment when they decide for themselves how to be.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. shaped.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause reads "the world has reached us and (2) ______ us" — the auxiliary has is shared by both verbs, so the blank needs the past participle (V3): *has reached and (has) shaped*. (वर्तमान पूर्ण काल)

◦ Shape here means to influence or mould a person's character, which fits "to a greater extent than we realize".

◦ Correct: …the world has reached us and shaped us to a greater extent than we realize.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "shapes" is a present-tense form and cannot follow the auxiliary *has*, breaking parallelism with "reached".

• "contours" is chiefly a noun (outlines); as a verb it is rare and would still need the -ed form here.

• "formats" means arranges in a particular layout — wrong in form (present tense) and wrong in sense for human character.

NOTE

• Parallel verbs after one auxiliary must all be V3: *She has sung and danced.*

• Collocations with shape: shape one's future, shape public opinion, take shape, in good shape.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By the (1) ______ we reach puberty, the world has reached us and (2) ______ us to a greater extent than we realize. (3) ______ family, friends, school, and society in general (4) ______ -by word and example-how to be. But people (5) ______ leaders at that moment when they decide for themselves how to be.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Our.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is written in the first person plural — "we reach puberty", "reached us", "than we realize" — so the possessive adjective must agree: Our family, friends, school…

◦ A possessive adjective (my, our, your, his, her, their) is required before the noun "family".

◦ Correct: Our family, friends, school, and society in general have told us…

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Their" shifts the person from *we/us* to a third party, destroying the pronoun consistency.

• "Her" is singular and third person, again inconsistent with "we/us".

• "There" is an adverb/introductory word, not a possessive adjective, so it cannot modify "family".

NOTE

• Homophone trap: their (possessive) / there (place) / they're (they are).

• Pronoun consistency: keep the same person throughout — *One must do one's duty*, not *their duty* in formal usage.

By the (1) ______ we reach puberty, the world has reached us and (2) ______ us to a greater extent than we realize. (3) ______ family, friends, school, and society in general (4) ______ -by word and example-how to be. But people (5) ______ leaders at that moment when they decide for themselves how to be.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. have told us.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject is a compound plural — "family, friends, school, and society in general" — so the plural auxiliary have is required. (कर्ता-क्रिया समन्वय)

◦ After *have*, the verb must be the past participle (V3) — told, giving the present perfect *have told*.

◦ "Tell" takes two objects: *tell us how to be* — the structure needs the active voice.

◦ Correct: Our family, friends, school, and society in general have told us — by word and example — how to be.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "have tell us" is wrong because *tell* (V1) cannot follow the auxiliary *have*.

• "has told us" uses a singular auxiliary with a plural compound subject.

• "have been told us" is a passive form; the subject here is the one doing the telling, and a passive cannot keep the object "us".

NOTE

• Subjects joined by and take a plural verb: *Ram and Shyam are friends.*

• V1–V2–V3: tell – told – told; teach – taught – taught; think – thought – thought.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By the (1) ______ we reach puberty, the world has reached us and (2) ______ us to a greater extent than we realize. (3) ______ family, friends, school, and society in general (4) ______ -by word and example-how to be. But people (5) ______ leaders at that moment when they decide for themselves how to be.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. begin to become.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subordinate clause uses the simple present — "when they decide for themselves" — so the main verb must also be simple present: begin. (काल की एकरूपता)

◦ After "begin", the to-infinitive takes the base form become, never the past form "became".

◦ Correct: But people begin to become leaders at that moment when they decide for themselves how to be.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "onset to became" is wrong on both counts — *onset* is a noun (beginning), and *became* cannot follow *to*.

• "began to become" is past tense and clashes with the present-tense clause "when they decide".

• "start to became" wrongly puts the past form *became* after the infinitive marker *to*.

NOTE

• Rule: to + V1 always (to go, to become), except in the phrase *used to*, *look forward to*, *object to* where *to* is a preposition and takes V-ing.

• *Begin/start* can take either the infinitive or the gerund: *begin to work* = *begin working*.

question: Which among the following statements is incorrect?
option_1: An increase in bank rate will decrease the money supply.
option_2: Lower the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), lower will be the liquidity in the system.
option_3: Higher the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), lower will be the liquidity in the system.
option_4: Lower the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), higher will be the liquidity in the system.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lower the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), lower will be the liquidity in the system.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• CRR is the percentage of a bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) that it must keep as cash reserves with the RBI. (नकद आरक्षित अनुपात)

• A lower CRR means banks retain more funds for lending, so liquidity in the system increases — hence statement 2 is factually wrong and is the answer.

• Statements 1, 3 and 4 are all correct: a higher bank rate makes borrowing costlier and contracts money supply; a higher CRR locks away more funds and reduces liquidity; a lower SLR frees funds and raises liquidity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bank Rate — the rate at which RBI lends long-term funds to banks without collateral; raising it is a contractionary measure.

• SLR — the share of NDTL banks must hold in liquid assets like cash, gold and approved government securities.

• CRR earns no interest for banks, while SLR assets do earn returns.

NOTE

• Quantitative tools of RBI: Bank Rate, Repo, Reverse Repo, CRR, SLR, OMO, MSF.

• Qualitative tools: margin requirements, moral suasion, credit rationing, direct action.

• Rule of thumb: CRR/SLR/Repo up → liquidity and money supply down.

question: ______ is the world's largest tropical rainforest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amazon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Amazon rainforest in South America is the world's largest tropical rainforest, covering about 5.5 million sq km across the Amazon basin. (अमेजन वर्षावन)

• It is often called the 'Lungs of the Earth' and is also known as Selvas; roughly 60% of it lies in Brazil, with parts in Peru, Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Bolivia, Guyana, Suriname and French Guiana.

• The Amazon river is the largest river in the world by discharge/volume of water and the second longest after the Nile.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Prairies — temperate grasslands of North America, not a rainforest.

• Daintree — an ancient tropical rainforest in Queensland, Australia, but far smaller than the Amazon.

• Congo rainforest — the world's second largest tropical rainforest, in the Congo Basin of Africa.

NOTE

• Grasslands one-liners: Prairies (North America), Pampas (Argentina), Steppes (Eurasia), Veld (South Africa), Downs (Australia), Llanos & Campos (South America).

• The Equator passes through the Amazon basin, giving it a hot, wet equatorial (Af) climate with rainfall throughout the year.

question: Which among the following are commonly known as blood thinners?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anticoagulants.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anticoagulants are drugs that slow down or prevent the clotting (coagulation) of blood, and are popularly called blood thinners. (रक्त पतला करने वाली दवाएँ)

• Common examples are heparin, warfarin, dabigatran and rivaroxaban; they are used to prevent thrombosis, stroke, deep vein thrombosis and clots in heart patients.

• Heparin also occurs naturally in the body and is used in stored blood to keep it from clotting.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Antibiotics — substances such as penicillin that kill or inhibit bacteria; they have no effect on viruses.

• Anticaking agents — food additives that stop powders like salt and milk powder from forming lumps.

• Antibodies — immunoglobulin proteins produced by B-lymphocytes that neutralise antigens.

NOTE

• Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting; anticoagulants like warfarin work by acting against vitamin K.

• Haemophilia is a hereditary disease in which blood fails to clot; blood group AB is the universal recipient and O negative the universal donor.

question: Which foreign invader surrendered his territories to Chandragupta Maurya?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seleucus Nicator.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Seleucus Nicator, a general of Alexander who ruled the eastern part of his empire, invaded India around 305 BCE and was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya. (सेल्यूकस निकेटर)

• By the resulting treaty (c. 303 BCE) Seleucus ceded Aria (Herat), Arachosia (Kandahar), Gedrosia (Baluchistan) and Paropanisadae (Kabul) to Chandragupta, and received 500 war elephants in return.

• He also sent Megasthenes as his ambassador to the Mauryan court at Pataliputra; Megasthenes wrote the account 'Indica'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Menander (Milinda) — Indo-Greek king who embraced Buddhism; his dialogue with monk Nagasena is recorded in the 'Milinda Panha'.

• Demosthenes — a famous Greek orator of Athens, not an invader of India.

• Gondophernes — an Indo-Parthian ruler of the 1st century CE, associated with St. Thomas.

NOTE

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire in 322 BCE with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the Arthashastra.

• He is said to have adopted Jainism and died at Shravanabelagola (Karnataka) by *sallekhana*, along with the Jain saint Bhadrabahu.

question: Sohan is suffering from goitre. Which deficiency is the most common cause of it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Deficiency of Iodine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Goitre is the abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland in the neck, and its most common cause worldwide is iodine deficiency. (घेंघा रोग)

• Iodine is needed to make the thyroid hormones thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3); without enough iodine the gland enlarges trying to trap more iodine.

• Prevention is by iodised salt, sea food and dairy products; India runs the National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme (NIDDCP).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Protein deficiency causes kwashiorkor and marasmus.

• Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness and xerophthalmia.

• Iron deficiency causes anaemia, since iron is needed for haemoglobin.

NOTE

• Deficiency diseases: Vitamin B1 — beri-beri; Vitamin B3 — pellagra; Vitamin C — scurvy; Vitamin D — rickets/osteomalacia; Vitamin K — poor blood clotting.

• The thyroid is the largest endocrine gland; excess secretion causes hyperthyroidism (Graves' disease) and low secretion causes cretinism in children and myxoedema in adults.

question: Which among the following is a covalent compound?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hydrogen chloride.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A covalent compound is formed by the sharing of electron pairs between atoms, usually between two non-metals. (सहसंयोजक यौगिक)

• In hydrogen chloride (HCl) a hydrogen atom shares one electron with a chlorine atom, forming a single covalent bond; both H and Cl are non-metals.

• The other three options are ionic compounds — formed by transfer of electrons between a metal and a non-metal or polyatomic ion.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Magnesium hydroxide Mg(OH)2 — ionic; used as an antacid, 'milk of magnesia'.

• Calcium carbonate CaCO3 — ionic; the chief constituent of limestone, marble and chalk.

• Sodium chloride NaCl — the classic ionic compound, common salt.

NOTE

• Covalent compounds generally have low melting/boiling points, are poor conductors and are usually insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.

• Ionic compounds are hard, brittle solids with high melting points that conduct electricity in molten or aqueous state.

• Note: gaseous HCl is covalent, but dissolved in water it ionises to give hydrochloric acid.

question: "And then One Day: A Memoir" is an autobiography of which of the following Bollywood star?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Naseeruddin Shah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'And Then One Day: A Memoir' (published 2014) is the autobiography of veteran actor Naseeruddin Shah. (आत्मकथा)

• The book covers his early years, his training at the National School of Drama (NSD) and the FTII, Pune, and his career in parallel cinema.

• Naseeruddin Shah has won three National Film Awards and has been honoured with the Padma Shri (1987) and Padma Bhushan (2003).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Karan Johar — wrote 'An Unsuitable Boy' (2017).

• Priyanka Chopra — wrote 'Unfinished' (2021).

• Shah Rukh Khan has not written an autobiography; 'King of Bollywood' by Anupama Chopra is a biography of him.

NOTE

• Other film autobiographies frequently asked: 'Romancing with Life' — Dev Anand; 'The Substance and the Shadow' — Dilip Kumar; 'Khullam Khulla' — Rishi Kapoor; 'I'll Do It My Way' — Sanjay Khan; 'The Making of a Legend' — Balraj Sahni.

• Naseeruddin Shah's notable films: Sparsh, Masoom, Jaane Bhi Do Yaaro, Ijaazat, A Wednesday.

question: In the sport of ______, two teams of five players each attempt to score points by putting the ball into a hoop that is 10 feet off the ground.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Basketball.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Basketball is played between two teams of five players each, who score by shooting the ball through a hoop fixed 10 feet (3.05 m) above the ground. (बास्केटबॉल)

• It was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891 at Springfield, Massachusetts, USA.

• The world governing body is FIBA (1932), headquartered at Mies, Switzerland; basketball became an Olympic sport in 1936 (Berlin).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Badminton — singles or doubles, played with a shuttlecock; governing body BWF.

• Rugby — 15 players a side in rugby union, 13 in rugby league; oval ball.

• Lawn tennis — singles (1) or doubles (2) players a side; governing body ITF.

NOTE

• Players per side: Cricket 11, Football 11, Hockey 11, Volleyball 6, Basketball 5, Kabaddi 7, Kho-Kho 9, Water polo 7, Polo 4.

• Basketball terms: dribble, dunk, rebound, free throw, layup, travelling, pivot.

question: The Superintendence, control and conduct of all election to the municipalities is responsibility of the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is State Election Commission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 243ZA of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to the municipalities in the State Election Commission. (राज्य निर्वाचन आयोग)

• The parallel provision for Panchayats is Article 243K; both were inserted by the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992.

• The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor, and can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of a High Court.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Election Commission of India (Article 324) conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President — not local bodies.

• The Governor appoints the State Election Commissioner but does not conduct the polls.

• Municipalities are covered by Part IXA (Articles 243P–243ZG) and the Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects).

NOTE

• 73rd Amendment — Panchayats, Part IX, Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects).

• 74th Amendment — Municipalities, Part IXA, Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects); both came into force in 1993.

• Three types of urban bodies: Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, Municipal Corporation.

question: Which festival marks the triumph of Goddess Durga over the demon king Mahishasura?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Navratri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Navratri (nine nights) celebrates the victory of Goddess Durga over the buffalo-demon Mahishasura, culminating in Vijayadashami/Dussehra on the tenth day. (नवरात्रि)

• The nine forms of the goddess worshipped are the Navadurga — Shailaputri, Brahmacharini, Chandraghanta, Kushmanda, Skandamata, Katyayani, Kalaratri, Mahagauri and Siddhidatri.

• Sharad Navratri falls in Ashwin (Sept–Oct); it is marked by Garba and Dandiya in Gujarat and Durga Puja in West Bengal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Diwali — celebrates Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya after defeating Ravana; festival of lights.

• Janmashtami — birth anniversary of Lord Krishna, in the month of Bhadrapada.

• Holi — festival of colours linked to Holika and Prahlada, celebrated on Phalguna Purnima.

NOTE

• The Durga Puja of Kolkata was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2021.

• Durga's exploits are described in the Devi Mahatmya (Durga Saptashati), part of the Markandeya Purana.

question: Who launched the SAMRIDDHI (Strengthening and Augmentation of Municipal Revenue for Infrastructure Development) scheme in October 2022 for Delhi, India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lieutenant Governor of Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• SAMRIDDHI 2022-23 — 'Strengthening and Augmentation of Municipal Revenue for Infrastructure Development in Delhi' — was launched in October 2022 by the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, Shri Vinai Kumar Saxena. (समृद्धि योजना)

• It is a one-time property tax amnesty scheme of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) allowing defaulters to clear dues by paying the principal tax of the current and previous five years, with interest and penalty waived.

• The aim was to improve the MCD's revenue base for urban infrastructure and to reduce litigation over old property-tax arrears.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Delhi is a Union Territory with a legislature (NCT); the Lieutenant Governor is its administrator under Article 239AA.

• The three erstwhile municipal corporations of Delhi were re-unified into a single MCD in May 2022 by the Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Act, 2022.

• Vinai Kumar Saxena took charge as Delhi's LG in May 2022.

NOTE

• Article 239AA was inserted by the 69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991, giving Delhi a Legislative Assembly and Council of Ministers.

• Property tax, advertisement tax and toll are important own-revenue sources of urban local bodies.

question: Who was the founder of Dharma Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Radhakanta Deb.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dharma Sabha was founded in 1830 at Calcutta by Raja Radhakanta Deb, as an orthodox organisation to counter the reformist Brahmo Samaj. (धर्म सभा)

• Its chief aim was to oppose the abolition of Sati by Lord William Bentinck's Regulation XVII of 1829; it even sent an appeal to the Privy Council in London, which was rejected in 1832.

• Despite being socially conservative, Radhakanta Deb supported Western education and female education.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy — founded the Atmiya Sabha (1814) and the Brahmo Samaj (1828); campaigned for the abolition of Sati.

• Dadoba Pandurang — associated with the Paramahansa Mandali (1849) and Manav Dharma Sabha in Maharashtra.

• R.G. Bhandarkar — a leader of the Prarthana Samaj and a noted Orientalist scholar.

NOTE

• Socio-religious reform bodies: Brahmo Samaj (1828, Ram Mohan Roy), Arya Samaj (1875, Dayanand Saraswati), Prarthana Samaj (1867, Atmaram Pandurang), Ramakrishna Mission (1897, Swami Vivekananda), Theosophical Society (1875, Blavatsky & Olcott).

• Sati was abolished in 1829 and Widow Remarriage legalised in 1856 through the efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

question: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma is known to create the formal structure and ornamentation of the ______ dance form.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma (1915–1999) is revered as the 'mother of Mohiniyattam' for reviving the dance and giving it a formal structure, repertoire and ornamentation. (मोहिनीअट्टम)

• Mohiniyattam is a classical solo dance of Kerala, performed by women; the name means the 'dance of the enchantress Mohini'.

• It is marked by gentle, swaying lasya movements, off-white kasavu costume with gold border, and songs in Manipravalam set to Sopana style music.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kathakali — the vigorous tandava-style dance-drama of Kerala with elaborate make-up (*chutti*) and masks.

• Bharatanatyam — classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra, also called the 'fire dance'.

• Kuchipudi — classical dance-drama of Andhra Pradesh, associated with Siddhendra Yogi and the Tarangam on a brass plate.

NOTE

• Eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (AP), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

• Other Mohiniyattam exponents: Sunanda Nair, Bharati Shivaji, Kanak Rele.

question: With respect to human geography, TFR stands for ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Total Fertility Rate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• TFR (Total Fertility Rate) is the average number of children a woman would bear during her entire reproductive span (15–49 years) at prevailing age-specific fertility rates. (कुल प्रजनन दर)

• A TFR of about 2.1 is called the replacement level fertility, at which a population just replaces itself.

• As per NFHS-5 (2019-21), India's TFR fell to 2.0, below replacement level for the first time; Bihar had the highest TFR (2.98) and Sikkim the lowest (1.1).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Crude Birth Rate (CBR) — live births per 1,000 population per year.

• Sex Ratio — number of females per 1,000 males (Census 2011: 943; NFHS-5: 1,020).

• IMR — infant deaths per 1,000 live births in a year.

NOTE

• Census 2011: population 121.08 crore, decadal growth 17.7%, density 382 persons/sq km, child sex ratio 919.

• The National Family Health Survey (NFHS) is conducted by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with IIPS Mumbai as the nodal agency.

question: "Bombay" Jayashri Ramnath is a famous ______ singer of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carnatic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bombay Jayashri Ramnath is a celebrated Carnatic vocalist of India. (कर्नाटक संगीत)

• She was nominated for the Academy Award (Oscar) for Best Original Song in 2013 for 'Pi's Lullaby' from the film Life of Pi, which she wrote and sang.

• She has been honoured with the Padma Shri (2021) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (2018).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Carnatic music is the classical music tradition of South India; Hindustani music is that of North India.

• The Trinity of Carnatic music — Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Shyama Shastri.

• Purandara Dasa is called the 'Father of Carnatic music'.

NOTE

• Famous Carnatic vocalists: M. S. Subbulakshmi (first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna, 1998), Balamuralikrishna, Sudha Raghunathan, T. M. Krishna (Magsaysay Award 2016).

• Carnatic music is based on raga and tala, with 72 Melakarta ragas as the parent scales.

question: Panthi dance form is associated with ______ state of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Panthi is a devotional folk dance of the Satnami community of Chhattisgarh, performed mainly on Guru Ghasidas Jayanti (Magh Purnima). (पंथी नृत्य)

• The dance is performed by men around a jaitkhamb (a white flag-post), with songs praising Guru Ghasidas and the Satnam philosophy, accompanied by the mandar and jhanjh.

• It begins slowly and builds up to a fast tempo with acrobatic human pyramids.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Maharashtra — Lavani, Tamasha, Powada, Dhangari Gaja.

• Kerala — Kaikottikali, Thiruvathirakali, Ottamthullal, Theyyam.

• Punjab — Bhangra, Giddha, Jhumar, Karthi.

NOTE

• Other folk dances of Chhattisgarh: Raut Nacha, Karma, Saila, Suwa, Pandwani (narrative folk singing, popularised by Teejan Bai).

• Folk dance one-liners: Garba — Gujarat; Bihu — Assam; Chhau — Jharkhand/Odisha/West Bengal; Ghoomar — Rajasthan; Rouf — Jammu & Kashmir.

question: Who among the following was a famous ruler of the Pandya dynasty of South India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nedunjeliyan II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nedunjeliyan II was a famous ruler of the Pandya dynasty of ancient South India, celebrated in Sangam literature. (पांड्य वंश)

• He is credited with the victory at the battle of Talaiyalanganam, where he defeated the combined forces of the Cholas, Cheras and five minor chieftains.

• The Pandyas ruled from Madurai with Korkai as their port; their emblem was the fish (carp) and they were known for pearl trade.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Karikala — the greatest Chola ruler of the Sangam age, famous for the battle of Venni and the Kallanai (Grand Anicut) dam on the Kaveri.

• Ashoka — the Mauryan emperor (c. 268–232 BCE), who embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga war.

• Nizam Shah — the dynastic title of the rulers of Ahmadnagar in medieval Deccan.

NOTE

• Sangam-age kingdoms and emblems: Chera — bow and arrow, capital Vanji, port Muziris; Chola — tiger, capital Uraiyur, port Puhar (Kaveripattinam); Pandya — fish, capital Madurai, port Korkai.

• The three Sangams were held under Pandya patronage at Madurai; Tolkappiyam is the oldest extant Tamil grammar.

question: Part XVI of the Indian constitution deals with ______.
option_2: Special provisions related to certain classes
option_4: Special provisions related to municipal corporation
solution_text:
The correct answer is Special provisions related to certain classes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part XVI (Articles 330–342) of the Constitution is titled 'Special Provisions Relating to Certain Classes'. (कुछ वर्गों के संबंध में विशेष उपबंध)

• It provides for reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha (Art. 330) and State Legislative Assemblies (Art. 332), reservation of posts/claims of SCs and STs in services (Art. 335), and the appointment of a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Art. 350B, which lies in Part XVII (Official Language).

• Article 338 — National Commission for SCs; Article 338A — National Commission for STs; Article 340 — Commission to investigate conditions of backward classes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Part XV (Articles 324–329) — Elections, including the Election Commission of India.

• Part XX (Article 368) — Amendment of the Constitution.

• Part IXA (Articles 243P–243ZG) — Municipalities.

NOTE

• Key Parts: Part III — Fundamental Rights; Part IV — DPSP; Part IVA — Fundamental Duties; Part V — Union; Part VI — States; Part XI — Centre-State relations; Part XVIII — Emergency provisions.

• Article 338B (National Commission for Backward Classes) was added by the 102nd Amendment Act, 2018.

question: According to Census 2011, what is the total literacy rate in India (approximately)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 74%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, India's overall literacy rate was 74.04% — approximately 74%. (साक्षरता दर)

• Male literacy was 82.14% and female literacy 65.46%, a gap of about 17 percentage points.

• A person aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language is counted as literate.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kerala had the highest literacy rate (94%) and Bihar the lowest (61.8%) in Census 2011.

• Among UTs, Lakshadweep ranked highest (91.8%); the district with the highest literacy was Serchhip (Mizoram).

• Census 2001 literacy was 64.8%, so the decade saw a rise of about 9 percentage points.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th since Independence; its slogan was 'Our Census, Our Future'.

• Other Census 2011 figures: population 121.08 crore, sex ratio 943, density 382/sq km, decadal growth 17.7%; Uttar Pradesh most populous, Sikkim least.

question: The Hindu College was established in Benaras in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1791.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hindu College (Sanskrit College) at Benaras was established in 1791 by Jonathan Duncan, the British Resident of Benaras. (बनारस संस्कृत कॉलेज)

• Its purpose was the study and preservation of Hindu law, literature and Sanskrit learning, partly to help the British administer Hindu personal law.

• It later grew into the Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi, and today is the Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (renamed 1974).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• 1781 — Calcutta Madrasa founded by Warren Hastings for the study of Muslim law.

• 1784 — Asiatic Society of Bengal founded by Sir William Jones.

• 1817 — Hindu College, Calcutta founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, David Hare and others; it later became Presidency College.

NOTE

• Education landmarks: Charter Act 1813 (Rs 1 lakh for education), Macaulay's Minute 1835 (English education), Wood's Despatch 1854 (Magna Carta of English education in India), Hunter Commission 1882, Universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras 1857.

• Banaras Hindu University (BHU) was founded separately in 1916 by Madan Mohan Malaviya.

question: Which Indian cricketer is also known as 'The Wall'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rahul Dravid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rahul Dravid is nicknamed 'The Wall' for his rock-solid defensive technique and immense powers of concentration in Test cricket. (द वॉल)

• He scored over 13,000 Test runs and 10,000 ODI runs, and holds the record for the most catches by a fielder in Tests (210).

• He was named ICC Player of the Year and Test Player of the Year in 2004, received the Padma Bhushan (2013), and coached the Indian team to the ICC T20 World Cup title in 2024.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kapil Dev — the 'Haryana Hurricane', captain of India's 1983 World Cup-winning team.

• Sachin Tendulkar — the 'Master Blaster'/'Little Master', only cricketer with 100 international centuries and a Bharat Ratna (2014).

• M. S. Dhoni — 'Captain Cool', led India to the 2007 T20 World Cup, 2011 ODI World Cup and 2013 Champions Trophy.

NOTE

• Other nicknames: Virender Sehwag — Najafgarh ka Nawab/Multan ka Sultan; Yuvraj Singh — Sixer King; Sourav Ganguly — Dada/Prince of Kolkata; Jhulan Goswami — Chakda Express.

• Dravid and V. V. S. Laxman shared the famous 376-run partnership at Eden Gardens against Australia in 2001.

question: Which among the following crops is an example of Kharif crop?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kharif crops are sown with the onset of the south-west monsoon (June–July) and harvested in September–October. (खरीफ फसल)

• Rice (paddy) is the leading kharif crop of India; it needs high temperature (above 25°C), high humidity and rainfall above 100 cm.

• Other kharif crops: maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, jute, groundnut, soyabean, tur (arhar), sugarcane.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Wheat, barley and mustard are Rabi crops, sown in October–December and harvested in April–June.

• Rabi crops need a cool growing season and a bright sunny period at ripening; western disturbances aid their winter rainfall.

• Zaid crops are grown between Rabi and Kharif (March–June): watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables and fodder.

NOTE

• West Bengal is the largest rice-producing state; Uttar Pradesh leads in wheat and sugarcane.

• India's Green Revolution (1960s) under M. S. Swaminathan and Norman Borlaug chiefly boosted wheat and rice output.

question: As of November 2022, who is the Speaker of Lok Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Om Birla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Om Birla, MP from Kota (Rajasthan), was elected Speaker of the 17th Lok Sabha in June 2019 and was serving as Speaker as of November 2022. (लोकसभा अध्यक्ष)

• The Speaker is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha from among themselves; he presides over its sittings, decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill (Article 110), and votes only in case of a tie (casting vote).

• The Speaker is removable by a resolution passed by an effective majority after 14 days' notice (Article 94).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Droupadi Murmu — took office as the 15th President of India in July 2022; first tribal woman President.

• Narendra Modi — the Prime Minister of India since 2014.

• Amit Shah — the Union Home Minister since 2019.

NOTE

• G. V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha; Meira Kumar was the first woman Speaker.

• The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Article 64); the Deputy Speaker is also elected by the Lok Sabha (Article 93).

question: Which is a major tributary of Bhagirathi river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhilangna.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bhilangna is the major tributary of the Bhagirathi, joining it at Old Tehri in Uttarakhand, where the Tehri Dam now stands. (भिलंगना नदी)

• The Bhagirathi rises from the Gaumukh snout of the Gangotri glacier at an altitude of about 3,892 m.

• At Devprayag, the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda, and from there the river is called the Ganga.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Dhauliganga — meets the Alaknanda at Vishnuprayag.

• Pindar — meets the Alaknanda at Karnaprayag.

• The other Alaknanda confluences: Nandprayag (Nandakini), Rudraprayag (Mandakini).

NOTE

• Panch Prayag of Uttarakhand: Vishnuprayag, Nandprayag, Karnaprayag, Rudraprayag, Devprayag.

• Left-bank tributaries of the Ganga: Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, Mahananda; right-bank: Yamuna, Son, Punpun.

• The Tehri Dam on the Bhagirathi is India's tallest dam (260.5 m).

question: How many UNESCO Natural World Heritage sites are there in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seven.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India has seven natural UNESCO World Heritage Sites. (प्राकृतिक विश्व धरोहर स्थल)

• They are: Kaziranga National Park (Assam), Manas Wildlife Sanctuary (Assam), Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan), Sundarbans National Park (West Bengal), Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks (Uttarakhand), Western Ghats, and Great Himalayan National Park (Himachal Pradesh).

• Kaziranga, Manas and Keoladeo were inscribed in 1985, the Sundarbans in 1987, the Western Ghats in 2012 and the Great Himalayan National Park in 2014.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India also has one mixed site — Khangchendzonga National Park, Sikkim (2016).

• The rest of India's World Heritage Sites are cultural, such as the Taj Mahal, Ajanta and Ellora Caves, Sun Temple Konark, Qutub Minar and Jaipur City.

• India's first World Heritage Sites (1983) were the Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Agra Fort and Taj Mahal.

NOTE

• UNESCO was established in 1945 and is headquartered in Paris, France; the World Heritage Convention was adopted in 1972.

• Kaziranga is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros; Keoladeo (Bharatpur) is a bird sanctuary and a Ramsar site.
